   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Recent accounting pronouncements </span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> Income Taxes (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>): Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures. This ASU requires disclosure of specific categories in the rate reconciliation and additional information for reconciling items that meet a quantitative threshold. The amendment also includes other changes to improve the effectiveness of income tax disclosures, including further disaggregation of income taxes paid for individually significant jurisdictions. This ASU is effective for annual periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2024. </em>Early adoption is permitted. Adoption of this ASU should be applied on a prospective basis, although retrospective application is permitted. The Company adopted the ASU on its consolidated financial statements and disclosures- see note <em style="font: inherit;">6.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> Income Statement&#8212;Reporting Comprehensive Income&#8212;Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>), Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses. This update aims to enhance the transparency of financial reporting by requiring public business entities (PBEs) to provide disaggregated disclosure of certain income statement expense captions into specified categories in disclosures within the footnotes to the financial statements. The ASU is effective for annual fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods within fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>Early adoption is permitted. Adoption of this ASU should be applied on a prospective basis, although retrospective application is permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of adopting this ASU on its consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2025 </em>the FASB issued&#160;ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em> &#8211; Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>): Measurement of Credit Losses for Accounts Receivable and Contract Assets, which provides a practical expedient for estimating expected credit losses on current accounts receivable and current contract assets arising from transactions accounted for under Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606</em> &#8211; Revenue from Contracts with Customers. Under this practical expedient, entities <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>assume that current conditions as of the balance sheet date do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> change for the remaining life of the asset. The ASU is effective for financial statements issued for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2025. </em>Early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of adopting this ASU on its consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Contract Assets &amp; Liabilities</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Contract assets are established when revenues are recognized prior to a contractual payment due from the customer. When a payment becomes due based on the contract terms, the Company will reduce the contract asset and record a receivable. Contract liabilities are deferred revenues that are recorded when cash payments are received or due in advance of our performance obligations. Our payment terms vary by the type and location of the products offered. The term between invoicing and when payment is due is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> significant.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#160;Assets held for sale</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 10, 2025, </em>as part of the Company&#8217;s ongoing strategy to focus on its core operations and optimize its asset base utilization, the Company completed the sale of its manufacturing facility located at Kent, Washington which was part of the Weighing Solutions Segment. The total sale proceeds amounted to $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654016" contextRef="i_2025-07-10_DisposalGroupClassificationAxis-DisposalGroupDisposedOfBySaleNotDiscontinuedOperationsMember_IncomeStatementBalanceSheetAndAdditionalDisclosuresByDisposalGroupsIncludingDiscontinuedOperationsAxis-ManufacturingFacilityInKentWashingtonMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DisposalGroupIncludingDiscontinuedOperationConsideration" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">11.5</ix:nonFraction> million, and the net proceeds, after deducting broker&#8217;s commission and real estate excise tax, were approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654017" contextRef="d_2025-07-10_2025-07-10_DisposalGroupClassificationAxis-DisposalGroupDisposedOfBySaleNotDiscontinuedOperationsMember_IncomeStatementBalanceSheetAndAdditionalDisclosuresByDisposalGroupsIncludingDiscontinuedOperationsAxis-ManufacturingFacilityInKentWashingtonMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromSaleOfProductiveAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">10.8</ix:nonFraction> million. The carrying amount of the asset was previously classified as asset held for sale under current assets in the consolidated balance sheet as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024 </em>after meeting the criteria outlined in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">360.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> further depreciation was recorded once the asset was classified as held for sale. The net cash proceeds were used to repay a portion of the Company's credit facility, as further discussed in Note <em style="font: inherit;">7</em>&#160;&#8211; Long-Term Debt. Upon completion of the sale, the Company recognized a gain of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654021" contextRef="d_2025-07-10_2025-07-10_DisposalGroupClassificationAxis-DisposalGroupDisposedOfBySaleNotDiscontinuedOperationsMember_IncomeStatementBalanceSheetAndAdditionalDisclosuresByDisposalGroupsIncludingDiscontinuedOperationsAxis-ManufacturingFacilityInKentWashingtonMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DisposalGroupNotDiscontinuedOperationGainLossOnDisposal" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.5</ix:nonFraction> million in <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2025, </em>which is included in Operating income in the condensed consolidated statements of operations for the&#160;Twelve Months Ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31,</em>&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>.</p>

   &#160;
  </div>
  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3114120" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">4</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#8211;</span><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">four</em> reporting units to which goodwill was allocated: steel, on-board weighing, DSI, and DTS. In <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> the Company performed a quantitative impairment test for all its reporting units. In estimating the fair value of our reporting units the Company used the income approach. The income approach to valuation requires management to make significant estimates and assumptions related to future revenues, profitability, working capital requirements and selection of discount rate and long term growth rate. Changes in these estimates and assumptions could have a significant impact on the fair value of the reporting units. If the fair value exceeds the carrying value, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> further evaluation is required and <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> impairment loss is recognized. An impairment charge would be recognized to the extent the carrying value of goodwill exceeds the reporting unit fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company's required&#160;goodwill and indefinite-lived asset annual impairment test is completed as of the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> day of the <em style="font: inherit;">fourth</em> fiscal quarter each year. In <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, the results of the quantitative impairment test for all reporting units indicated that the fair value of the reporting units exceeded their carrying values, and therefore <ix:nonFraction id="c140654033" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetImpairment" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> impairment was recognized.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">5</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#160;Restructuring Costs</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Restructuring costs reflect the cost reduction programs implemented by the Company. Restructuring costs are expensed during the period in which the Company determines it will incur those costs and all requirements for accrual are met. Because these costs are recorded based upon estimates, actual expenditures for the restructuring activities <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>differ from the initially recorded costs. If the initial estimates are too low or too high, the Company could be required to either record additional expense in future periods or to reverse part of the previously recorded charges.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company recorded restructuring costs of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654044" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million,&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140654045" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654046" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million during the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively. The restructuring costs were comprised primarily of employee termination costs, including severance and statutory retirement allowances, and were incurred in connection with various cost reduction programs.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">6</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Income Taxes</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company is subject to U.S. federal tax at the rate of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c140654053" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">21</ix:nonFraction>%.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 22, 2017, </em>the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the "Tax Act") was signed into law making significant changes to U.S. income tax law.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">On&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;"> July 4, 2025,</em></i>&#160;the OBBBA&#160;was enacted into law, extending key provisions of the&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">2017</em></i>&#160;Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. The OBBBA restores expensing of domestic research expenditures for years beginning after&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024.</em></i>&#160;Additionally, the OBBBA restores the EBITDA-based interest expense limitation and includes changes related to the U.S. taxation of the income of our foreign subsidiaries and certain foreign derived income, and the base erosion and anti-abuse tax, and provides for accelerated depreciation for property acquired and placed in service after&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;"> January 19, 2025.</em></i>&#160;The legislation has multiple effective dates, with certain provisions effective in&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em></i>&#160;and others implemented through&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">2027.</em></i>&#160;Due to the OBBBA provisions, the Company recorded tax benefit for the year as a decrease in valuation allowance on part of our deferred tax assets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The Company recognized approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654057" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="vpg:GlobalIntangibleLowTaxIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.6</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654058" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="vpg:GlobalIntangibleLowTaxIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of GILTI for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> respectively.&#160;The U.S. tax on&#160;Global Intangible Low-taxed Income ("GILTI"), net of foreign tax credits and other credits, was less than $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654060" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationGiltiAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for each of the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">6</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Income Taxes (continued)</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company established a valuation allowance with respect to substantially all of its U.S. deferred tax assets due to uncertainty regarding the realization of these assets. Throughout <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Company reassessed its ability to realize its U.S. and other deferred tax assets by considering both positive and negative evidence regarding realization. The most significant negative evidence is continuing cumulative operating losses in the U.S. The impact of its US companies acquisitions was also considered in determining the realization of the U.S. deferred tax assets. Other aspects, such as operating results, additional interest expense and additional tax deductions related to the acquisitions, were also considered. The Company also considered positive evidence such as tax planning strategies and the projected benefits of our restructuring efforts. However, there was insufficient positive evidence to overcome the negative evidence.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Overall, the cumulative losses and the acquisition impacts still indicate that realization of our U.S. deferred tax assets remains uncertain such that the Company cannot conclude that it is "more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not"</em> that the deferred tax assets will be recoverable.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We will continue to monitor the realization of U.S. deferred tax assets and reduce the valuation allowance if, and when, sufficient positive evidence of realization exists.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2024, </em>the Company acquired Nokra, a German entity. Nokra's opening balance sheet included&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140654081" contextRef="i_2024-09-30_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-NokraMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of gross deferred tax assets, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654082" contextRef="i_2024-09-30_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-NokraMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxLiabilitiesGoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsIntangibleAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of indefinite-lived liabilities as a result of the purchase price allocation. The acquisition contributed to a less than $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654083" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-NokraMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million net increase in valuation allowance and deferred tax expense for the Company in <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em> In <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Nokra&#8217;s valuation allowance net increase was $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654086" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-NokraMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 0pt;">At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> the valuation allowance on U.S. deferred tax assets was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654088" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">12.7</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654089" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">13.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively. The net change in this valuation allowance was approximately $(<ix:nonFraction id="c140654090" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">0.6</ix:nonFraction>)&#160;million, mostly related to net federal valuation allowances.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company also has valuation allowances of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654091" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-ForeignCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654092" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-ForeignCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively, with respect to certain foreign net operating loss and capital loss carryforwards.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Undistributed earnings of the Company&#8217;s foreign subsidiaries were approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654097" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UndistributedEarningsOfForeignSubsidiaries" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">304.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> compared to $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654098" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UndistributedEarningsOfForeignSubsidiaries" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">300.5</ix:nonFraction> million at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company had provided for a deferred tax liability of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654099" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxLiabilitiesInvestmentInNoncontrolledAffiliates" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of withholding tax associated with $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654100" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-SubsidiariesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Revenues" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">21</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of unremitted, non-permanently reinvested earnings. Substantially all of the remaining undistributed earnings are considered to be indefinitely reinvested and accordingly <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> provision has been made with respect to these earnings for incremental foreign income taxes, state income taxes or foreign withholding taxes. If those earnings were distributed to the U.S., the Company could be subject to incremental foreign income taxes, state income taxes, and withholding taxes. Determination of the amount of unrecognized deferred tax liability is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> practicable because of the uncertainty regarding the timing of any such distribution and the impact on existing valuation allowances. In addition to the <em style="font: inherit;">$2.1</em> million, additional withholding taxes of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654104" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxLiabilityNotRecognizedAmountOfUnrecognizedDeferredTaxLiabilityUndistributedEarningsOfForeignSubsidiaries" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">32.5</ix:nonFraction> million are estimated to be payable upon distribution of the remaining previously unremitted earnings as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company and its subsidiaries are subject to income taxes imposed by the U.S., various states, and the foreign jurisdictions in which we operate. Each jurisdiction establishes rules that set forth the years which are subject to examination by its tax authorities. While the Company believes the tax positions taken on its tax returns for each jurisdiction are supportable, they <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>still be challenged by the jurisdiction's tax authorities. In anticipation of such challenges, the Company has established reserves for tax-related uncertainties. These liabilities are based on the Company&#8217;s best estimate of the potential tax exposures in each respective jurisdiction. It <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>take a number of years for a final tax liability in a jurisdiction to be determined, particularly in the event of an audit. If an uncertain matter is determined favorably, there could be a reduction in the Company&#8217;s tax expense. An unfavorable determination could increase tax expense and could require a cash payment, including interest and penalties.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">6</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Income Taxes (continued)</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company recognizes accrued interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits as a component of income tax expense. Related to the unrecognized tax benefits noted above, for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, the Company accrued penalties and interest annually in a Insignificant amounts (lower than&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">$0.1</em>&#160;million&#160;annually). As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, accrued penalties and interest were $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654117" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncomeTaxPenaltiesAndInterestAccrued" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million, each year.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Included in the balance of unrecognized tax benefits as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> is $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654120" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsThatWouldImpactEffectiveTaxRate" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654121" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsThatWouldImpactEffectiveTaxRate" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654122" contextRef="i_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsThatWouldImpactEffectiveTaxRate" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.8</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, of tax benefits that, if recognized, would impact the effective tax rate. Furthermore, as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> anticipate that any of its current unrecognized tax benefits will reverse within the next calendar year due to the expiration of the statute of limitations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company and its subsidiaries file U.S. federal income tax returns, as well as income tax returns in various state, local, and foreign jurisdictions. The Company files federal, state, and local income tax returns on a combined, unitary, or stand-alone basis. The statute of limitations in those jurisdictions generally ranges from <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> to <em style="font: inherit;">4</em> years. Additionally, the Company's foreign subsidiaries file income tax returns in the countries in which they have operations and the statutes of limitations in those jurisdictions generally range from <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> to <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> years.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> a tax examination began of <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> its subsidiaries in Israel covering the years <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140654131">2019</span>-<em style="font: inherit;">2023.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> the Company concluded a tax examination in France for <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of its subsidiaries covering the years <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140654136">2021</span> and <em style="font: inherit;">2022,</em> which resulted in <ix:nonFraction id="c140654138" contextRef="d_2024-04-01_2024-06-30_IncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis-MinistryOfTheEconomyFinanceAndIndustryFranceMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationPenaltiesAndInterestExpense" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> change in tax.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">fourth</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> a tax examination began in Germany of <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> of the Company's subsidiaries. The Company also concluded a tax examination in Taiwan for <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of its subsidiaries covering the year <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140654143">2022,</span> which resulted in <ix:nonFraction id="c140654144" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2024-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis-FederalMinistryOfFinanceGermanyMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationPenaltiesAndInterestExpense" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> change in tax.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company is subject to ongoing income tax audits, administrative appeals and judicial proceedings in India spanning a number of years.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Credit Agreement</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> August 15, 2024, </em>the Company entered into a Fourth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2024</em> Credit Agreement&#8221;) among the Company, the lenders party thereto, JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and HSBC as joint lead arrangers and joint bookrunner, and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as agent for such lenders, pursuant to which its previously existing credit agreement, was amended and restated to, among other things, extend the maturity date from <em style="font: inherit;"> March 20, 2025 </em>to <em style="font: inherit;"> August 15, 2029 </em>and adjust the interest rate and commitment fee. The <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Credit Agreement provides for a multicurrency, secured credit facility (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2024</em> Revolving Facility&#8221;) in an aggregate principal amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654150" contextRef="i_2024-08-15_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2024CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">75.0</ix:nonFraction> million, with a sublimit of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654151" contextRef="i_2024-08-15_CreditFacilityAxis-LetterOfCreditMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2024CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">10</ix:nonFraction> million which can be used for letters of credit for the account of the Company or its subsidiaries that are parties to the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Credit Agreement, the proceeds of which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be used for working capital and general corporate purposes, and a portion of which were used to refinance the existing credit facility. The aggregate principal amount of the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Revolving Facility <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be increased by a maximum of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654154" contextRef="i_2024-08-15_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2024CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="vpg:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumIncreaseInBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">25.0</ix:nonFraction> million upon the request of the Company, subject to the terms of the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Credit Agreement. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>elect to make loans under the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Revolving Facility in US Dollars, Euros, Canadian Dollars, Sterling, Japanese Yen or such other freely convertible foreign currency.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">7</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Long-Term Debt (continued)</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Amounts borrowed under the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Revolving Facility accrue interest in an amount equal to a floating rate plus a specified margin. Such floating rates are (i) for loans denominated in US Dollars, at the Company&#8217;s option, either (a) the greatest of: the Agent&#8217;s prime rate, the Federal Funds rate, or a <ix:nonFraction id="c140654160" contextRef="d_2024-08-15_2024-08-15_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2024CreditAgreementMember_VariableRateAxis-BaseRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="vpg:DebtInstrumentFloatingRateFloor" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">1</ix:nonFraction>% floor (the &#8220;US Base Rate&#8221;), or (b) the SOFR, (ii) for loans denominated in Canadian Dollars, at the Company&#8217;s option, either (<em style="font: inherit;">x</em>) the greatest of: the PRIMCAN Index rate, the average <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> day rate for loans accruing interest based on the Canadian Overnight Repo Rate Average (&#8220;CORRA&#8221;) (the &#8220;Canadian Base Rate&#8221;), or (y) CORRA, (iii) for loans denominated in Pounds Sterling, the Sterling Overnight Index Average (&#8220;SONIA&#8221;), (iv) for loans denominated in Euros, the Euro Interbank Offered Rate (&#8220;EURIBOR"), and (v) for loans denominated in Japanese Yen, the Tokyo Interbank Offered Rate (&#8220;TIBOR&#8221;). The specified interest margin for US Base Rate Loans and Canadian Base Rate Loans is <ix:nonFraction id="c140654163" contextRef="d_2024-08-15_2024-08-15_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2024CreditAgreementMember_VariableRateAxis-BaseRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">0.25</ix:nonFraction>%. Depending upon the Company&#8217;s leverage ratio, the interest rate margin for loans based on SOFR, CORRA, SONIA, EURIBOR and TIBOR ranges from <ix:nonFraction id="c140654164" contextRef="d_2024-08-15_2024-08-15_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2024CreditAgreementMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember_VariableRateAxis-OtherApplicableRatesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">1.75</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction id="c140654165" contextRef="d_2024-08-15_2024-08-15_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2024CreditAgreementMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember_VariableRateAxis-OtherApplicableRatesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">3.00</ix:nonFraction>% per annum. The Company is required to pay a quarterly fee of <ix:nonFraction id="c140654166" contextRef="d_2024-08-15_2024-08-15_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2024CreditAgreementMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityUnusedCapacityCommitmentFeePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">0.20</ix:nonFraction>% per annum to <ix:nonFraction id="c140654167" contextRef="d_2024-08-15_2024-08-15_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2024CreditAgreementMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityUnusedCapacityCommitmentFeePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">0.40</ix:nonFraction>% per annum on the unused portion of the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Revolving Facility, which is also determined based on the Company&#8217;s leverage ratio. Additional customary fees apply with respect to letters of credit.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 17, 2025, </em>the Company made a partial repayment of the outstanding balance under the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Credit Agreement in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654170" contextRef="d_2025-07-17_2025-07-17_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2024CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfLinesOfCredit" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">11.0</ix:nonFraction> million, using proceeds from the sale of manufacturing facility (see Note <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> - Asset Held for Sale). The repayment was made in accordance with the terms of the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Credit Agreement and resulted in a corresponding reduction in the outstanding balance under the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Revolving Facility. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the outstanding balance under the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Revolving Facility was $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654175" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2024CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">20.6</ix:nonFraction> million, bearing interest at variable rates based on the Credit Agreement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The obligations of the Company under the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Credit Agreement are secured by pledges of stock in certain domestic and foreign subsidiaries, as well as guarantees by substantially all of the Company&#8217;s domestic subsidiaries. The obligations of the Company and the guarantors under the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Credit Agreement are secured by substantially all the assets (excluding real estate) of the Company and such guarantors. The <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Credit Agreement restricts the Company from paying cash dividends and requires the Company to comply with other customary covenants, representations, and warranties, including the maintenance of specific financial ratios. The financial maintenance covenants include an interest coverage ratio and a leverage ratio. The Company was in compliance with its financial maintenance covenants as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. If the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> in compliance with any of these covenant restrictions, the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Revolving Facility could be terminated by the lenders, and all amounts outstanding pursuant to the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Revolving Facility could become immediately payable.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">8</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Stockholders</span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8217;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Equity</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s Class B convertible common stock carries <em style="font: inherit;">ten</em> votes per share. The Company's&#160;common stock carries <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> vote per share. Class B shares are transferable only to certain permitted transferees. Class B shares are convertible on a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>- for-<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140654192">one</span> basis at any time into shares of common stock. Transfers of Class B shares other than to permitted transferees will result in the automatic conversion of the Class B shares into common stock.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Board of Directors <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>only declare dividends or other distributions with respect to the common stock or the Class B convertible common stock if it grants such dividends or distributions in the same amount per share with respect to the other class of stock. As discussed in Note <em style="font: inherit;">7,</em> the Company is restricted from paying cash dividends. Stock dividends or distributions, on any class of stock, are payable only in shares of stock of that class. Shares of either common stock or Class B convertible common stock cannot be split, divided, or combined unless the other is also split, divided, or combined equally.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">8</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Stockholders</span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8217;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Equity (continued)</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> August 8, 2022, </em>the Board of Directors of the Company authorized the repurchase of up to <ix:nonFraction id="c140654196" contextRef="i_2022-08-08_ShareRepurchaseProgramAxis-StockRepurchasePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="srt:StockRepurchaseProgramNumberOfSharesAuthorizedToBeRepurchased" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">600,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s outstanding common stock (the &#8220;Stock Repurchase Plan&#8221;). The Stock Repurchase Plan was originally set to expire on <em style="font: inherit;"> August 11, 2023, </em>and the Board authorized purchases thereunder to be made through an issuer repurchase plan adopted under Rule <em style="font: inherit;">10b5</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">1</em> of the Securities Exchange Act of <em style="font: inherit;">1934,</em> as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;), open market purchases or private transactions, in accordance with the applicable federal securities laws, including Rule <em style="font: inherit;">10b</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">18</em> under the Exchange Act. On <em style="font: inherit;"> August 8, 2023, </em>the Company announced that its Board of Directors extended the term of the previously approved stock repurchase plan to <em style="font: inherit;"> August 9, 2024. </em>The Stock Repurchase Plan expired in accordance with its terms on <em style="font: inherit;"> August 9, 2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">From <em style="font: inherit;"> August 8, 2022 </em>to <em style="font: inherit;"> August 9, 2024, </em>the Company had repurchased an aggregate of <ix:nonFraction id="c140654202" contextRef="d_2022-08-08_2024-08-09_ShareRepurchaseProgramAxis-StockRepurchasePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:TreasuryStockSharesAcquired" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">518,328</ix:nonFraction> shares of its common stock under the Stock Repurchase Plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Board of Directors is authorized, without further stockholder approval, to issue from time to time up to an aggregate of <ix:nonFraction id="c140654203" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of preferred stock in <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more series. The Board of Directors <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>fix or alter the designation, preferences, rights and any qualification, limitations, restrictions of the shares of any series, including the dividend rights, dividend rates, conversion rights, voting rights, redemption terms and prices, liquidation preferences and the number of shares constituting any series. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> shares of the Company&#8217;s preferred stock are currently outstanding.</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">9</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Pensions and Other Postretirement Benefits (continued)</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>U.S. Pension Plan</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Vishay Precision Group Non-Qualified Retirement Plan, like all non-qualified plans, is considered to be unfunded. The Company maintains a nonqualified trust, referred to as a &#8220;rabbi&#8221; trust, to fund benefits under this plan. Rabbi trust assets are subject to creditor claims under certain conditions and are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the property of employees. Therefore, they are accounted for as other noncurrent assets within the consolidated balance sheets. The assets held in the rabbi trust are invested in money market funds and company-owned life insurance policies. The consolidated balance sheets include assets held in trust related to the nonqualified pension plan of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654211" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssetsForPlanBenefitsNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654212" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssetsForPlanBenefitsNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, and the related liabilities of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654213" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansLiabilitiesCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654214" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansLiabilitiesCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Vishay Precision Group Non-Qualified Retirement Plan is frozen. Accordingly, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> new employees <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>participate in the plan, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> further participant contributions are permitted, and <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> further benefits accrue. Benefits accumulated prior to the freezing of the U.S. pension plan will be paid to employees upon retirement, and the Company will likely need to make additional cash contributions to the rabbi trust to fund this accumulated benefit obligation.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Non-U.S. Pension Plans</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company provides pension and similar benefits to employees of certain non-U.S. subsidiaries consistent with local practices. Pension benefits earned are generally based on years of service and compensation during active employment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   </ix:continuation>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The plans&#8217; expected return on assets is based on management&#8217;s expectation of long-term average rates of return to be achieved by the underlying investment portfolios. In establishing this assumption, management considers historical and expected returns for the asset classes in which the plans are invested, advice from pension consultants and investment advisors, and current economic and capital market conditions.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The investment mix between equity securities and fixed income securities is based upon achieving a desired return, balancing higher return, more volatile equity securities, and lower return, less volatile fixed income securities. The target allocation of plan assets approximates the actual allocation of plan assets at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company maintains defined benefit retirement plans in certain of its subsidiaries. The assets of the plans are measured at fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Equity securities held by the defined benefit retirement plans consist of equity securities that are valued based on quoted market prices on the last business day of the year. The fair value measurement of the equity securities is considered a Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> measurement within the fair value hierarchy.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Fixed income securities held by the defined benefit retirement plans consist of government bonds and corporate notes that are valued based on quoted market prices on the last business day of the year. The fair value measurement of the fixed income securities is considered a Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> measurement within the fair value hierarchy.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Cash held by the defined benefit retirement plans consists of deposits on account in various financial institutions. The carrying amount of the cash approximates its fair value. A summary of the Company&#8217;s pension plan assets for each fair value hierarchy level are as follows for the periods presented (see Note <em style="font: inherit;">16</em> for further description of the levels within the fair value hierarchy <i>(in thousands)</i>:</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Other Postretirement Benefit Plans</i></b></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Actuarial gains incurred in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> related to our post-retirement plans are primarily the result of the increase discount rate assumptions used to estimate the benefit obligation as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> compared to <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>.    </ix:continuation>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">As the plans are unfunded, the Company's anticipated contributions for <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> are equal to the estimated benefit payment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Other Retirement Obligations</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company participates in various other defined contribution plans based on local law or custom. The Company periodically makes contributions to these plans. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, the consolidated balance sheets include $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654256" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-OtherPostretirementBenefitPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansCurrentLiabilities" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654257" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-OtherPostretirementBenefitPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansCurrentLiabilities" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, within accrued pension and other postretirement costs related to these plans.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Most of the Company&#8217;s U.S. employees are eligible to participate in <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) savings plans which provide company matching under various formulas. The Company&#8217;s matching expense for the plans was $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654259" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-OtherPostretirementBenefitPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OtherPostretirementBenefitExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654260" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-OtherPostretirementBenefitPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OtherPostretirementBenefitExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.2</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654261" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-OtherPostretirementBenefitPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OtherPostretirementBenefitExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> material amounts are included in the consolidated balance sheets related to unfunded <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) contributions.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Certain key employees participate in a nonqualified deferred compensation plan, which allows these employees to defer a portion of their compensation until retirement, or elect shorter deferral periods. The accompanying consolidated balance sheets include a liability within other noncurrent liabilities related to these deferrals. The Company maintains a nonqualified trust, referred to as a &#8220;rabbi&#8221; trust, to fund payments under this plan. Rabbi trust assets are subject to creditor claims under certain conditions and are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the property of employees. Therefore, they are accounted for as other noncurrent assets within the consolidated balance sheets. The assets held in the rabbi trust are invested in money market funds and company-owned life insurance policies. The consolidated balance sheets include assets held in trust related to the nonqualified deferred compensation plan of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654267" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-OtherPostretirementBenefitPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssetsForPlanBenefitsNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">5.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654268" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-OtherPostretirementBenefitPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssetsForPlanBenefitsNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> respectively, and the related liabilities of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654270" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-OtherPostretirementBenefitPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansLiabilitiesCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">6.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654271" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-OtherPostretirementBenefitPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansLiabilitiesCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2024, </em>the UK Court of Appeal upheld a ruling in the matter of Virgin Media Limited versus NTL Pension Trustees II Limited, that certain historical amendments for contracted out defined benefit schemes were invalid if they were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> accompanied by the correct actuarial confirmation, a decision that the Company was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a party to or involved in and could impact the Company&#8217;s non US pension plan in the UK. The Company and its UK pension scheme trustee are reviewing this development, along with its actuaries, and considering whether this decision has any implications for its UK pension plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> June 2025, </em>the UK Department for Work and Pensions announced that the government will introduce legislation to give affected pension schemes the ability to retrospectively obtain written actuarial confirmation that historic benefit changes met the necessary standards. The Company and its UK pension scheme trustee are reviewing this development, along with our actuaries, and considering whether this decision has any implications for its UK pension plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160; &#160;</p>
