  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:DisclosureOfCompensationRelatedCostsShareBasedPaymentsTextBlock" id="c3114161" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>&#160;</span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Share-Based Compensation</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Vishay Precision Group, Inc. <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Stock Incentive Plan (the <em style="font: inherit;">"2022</em> plan") permits the issuance of up to <ix:nonFraction id="c140654279" contextRef="i_2022-12-31_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">608,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> the Company had reserved&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c140654280" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">378,739</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of common stock for future grant of equity awards (restricted stock, unrestricted stock, restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;), or stock options) pursuant to the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Plan. If any outstanding awards are forfeited by the holder or canceled by the Company, the underlying shares would be available for re-grant to others. If shares are withheld for payment of taxes, those shares do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> become available for future grant under the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Restricted Stock Units</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Pursuant to the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> plan, the Company issued RSUs to board members, executive officers, and certain employees of the Company during <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>. The amount of compensation cost related to share-based payment transactions is measured based on the grant-date fair value of the equity instruments issued. VPG determines compensation cost for RSUs based on the grant-date fair value of the underlying common stock. Compensation cost is recognized over the period that the participant provides service in exchange for the award. The Company recognizes compensation cost for RSUs that are expected to vest and for which performance criteria are expected to be met.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 25, 2025 </em>and in accordance with their respective employment agreements, VPG&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> executive officers were granted annual equity awards in the form of RSUs, of which <ix:nonFraction id="c140654287" contextRef="i_2025-02-25_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-ExecutiveOfficerMember" unitRef="Pure" name="vpg:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentagePerformancebased" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction>% are performance-based. The awards have an aggregate grant-date fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654288" contextRef="d_2025-02-25_2025-02-25_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-ExecutiveOfficerMember" unitRef="USD" name="vpg:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriodAggregateGrantDateFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.9</ix:nonFraction> million and were comprised of <ix:nonFraction id="c140654289" contextRef="d_2025-02-25_2025-02-25_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-ExecutiveOfficerMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">79,729</ix:nonFraction> RSUs. Fifty percent of these awards will vest on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2028, </em>subject to the executives&#8217; continued employment. The performance-based portion of the RSUs will also vest on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2028, </em>subject to the executives' continued employment and the satisfaction of certain performance objectives relating to <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year cumulative &#8220;adjusted free cash flow&#8221; and "net earnings goals", each weighted equally.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 25, 2025, </em>certain non-executive VPG employees were granted annual equity awards in the form of RSUs. Certain employees received awards, of which <ix:nonFraction id="c140654291" contextRef="i_2025-02-25_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-CertainEmployeesGroupOneMember" unitRef="Pure" name="vpg:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentagePerformancebased" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">75</ix:nonFraction>% are performance-based and certain employees received awards of which <ix:nonFraction id="c140654292" contextRef="i_2025-02-25_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-CertainEmployeesGroupTwoMember" unitRef="Pure" name="vpg:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentagePerformancebased" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction>% are performance-based. The awards have an aggregate grant-date fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654293" contextRef="d_2025-02-25_2025-02-25_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-NonExecutivesMember" unitRef="USD" name="vpg:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriodAggregateGrantDateFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million and were comprised of <ix:nonFraction id="c140654294" contextRef="d_2025-02-25_2025-02-25_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-NonExecutivesMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">18,282</ix:nonFraction> RSUs. The non-performance portion of these awards (<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140654295">twenty-five</span> percent for certain employees and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140654296">fifty</span> percent for certain employees) will vest on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2028, </em>subject to the employees' continued employment. The performance-based portion of the RSUs will also vest on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2028, </em>subject to the employees' continued employment and the satisfaction of certain performance objectives relating to <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year cumulative earnings and cash flow goals, each weighted equally.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 21, 2025, </em>and in accordance with the Company's <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Non-Employee Director Compensation Plan, the Board of Directors ("Board") approved the issuance of an aggregate of <ix:nonFraction id="c140654299" contextRef="d_2025-05-21_2025-05-21_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-NonExecutivesMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">18,252</ix:nonFraction> RSUs to the independent board members of the Board. The awards had an aggregate grant-date fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654300" contextRef="d_2025-05-21_2025-05-21_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-NonExecutivesMember" unitRef="USD" name="vpg:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriodAggregateGrantDateFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.5</ix:nonFraction> million and will vest on or before the <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Annual Stockholders Meeting in <em style="font: inherit;"> May 2026, </em>subject to each applicable director's continued service on the Board. Vesting of equity awards is subject to acceleration under certain circumstances.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2025, </em>certain non-executive VPG employees were granted annual equity awards in the form of RSUs. One employee received an award, of which <ix:nonFraction id="c140654302" contextRef="i_2025-07-01_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-CertainEmployeesGroupOneMember" unitRef="Pure" name="vpg:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentagePerformancebased" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">75</ix:nonFraction>% is performance-based and <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> employee received an award of which <ix:nonFraction id="c140654304" contextRef="i_2025-07-01_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-CertainEmployeesGroupTwoMember" unitRef="Pure" name="vpg:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentagePerformancebased" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction>% is performance-based. The awards have an aggregate grant-date fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654305" contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2025-07-01_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-NonExecutivesMember" unitRef="USD" name="vpg:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriodAggregateGrantDateFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million and were comprised of <ix:nonFraction id="c140654306" contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2025-07-01_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-NonExecutivesMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,444</ix:nonFraction> RSUs. The non-performance portion of these awards will vest on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2028, </em>subject to the employees' continued employment. The performance-based portion of the RSUs will also vest on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2028, </em>subject to the employees' continued employment and the satisfaction of certain performance objectives relating to <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year cumulative earnings and cash flow goals, each weighted equally.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">11</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Commitments, Contingencies, and Concentrations</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i><b>Tax Assessment</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> the Israeli Tax Authority has issued a Value Added Tax (VAT) assessment to the Company, in the amount of ILS <ix:nonFraction id="c140654353" contextRef="d_2024-03-30_2024-06-29_IncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis-IsraelTaxAuthorityMember_LitigationCaseAxis-ValueAddedTaxAssessmentMember" unitRef="ILS" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8.4</ix:nonFraction> million (approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654354" contextRef="d_2024-03-30_2024-06-29_IncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis-IsraelTaxAuthorityMember_LitigationCaseAxis-ValueAddedTaxAssessmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.6</ix:nonFraction> million), pertaining to claims of VAT between the years <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> to <em style="font: inherit;">2023.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> August 6, 2025, </em>the Company received the decision of the Israeli Tax Authority regarding the Company's appeal of the VAT assessment. The appeal was rejected, based on the same reasoning outlined in the original assessment issued to the Company. The Company deferred the assessment and with the assistance of its legal counsel appealed on this decision to the court&#160;on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 18, 2026.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company believes that the liability for the assessment is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> probable, and given the stage of this matter, the Company is currently unable to predict the likely outcome or estimate the potential financial impact, if any, of this matter.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Litigation</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company is subject to various legal proceedings that constitute ordinary, routine litigation incidental to its business. The Company is of the opinion that the disposition of these proceedings will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on its business or its financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Executive Employment Agreements</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company has employment agreements with its executive officers which outline base salary, incentive compensation, and equity-based compensation. The employment agreements with the Company's executive officers also provide for incremental compensation in the event of termination without cause or resignation for good reason.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Sources of Supplies</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Although most materials incorporated in the Company&#8217;s products are available from a number of sources, certain materials are available only from a relatively limited number of suppliers.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Some of the most highly specialized materials for the Company&#8217;s sensors are sourced from a single vendor. The Company maintains a safety stock inventory of certain critical materials at its facilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Certain metals used in the manufacture of the Company&#8217;s products are traded on active markets, and can be subject to significant price volatility.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">11</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Commitments, Contingencies, and Concentrations (continued)</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Market Concentrations</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><em style="font: inherit;">No</em> single customer comprises greater than <em style="font: inherit;">10%</em> of net revenues.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The vast majority of the Company&#8217;s products are used in the broad industrial market, with selected uses in military and aerospace, medical, agriculture, and construction. Within the broad industrial segment, the Company&#8217;s products serve wide applications in the waste management, bulk hauling, logging, scale manufacturing, engineering systems, pharmaceutical, oil, chemical, steel, paper, and food industries.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Credit Risk Concentrations</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Financial instruments with potential credit risk consist principally of cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable, and notes receivable. The Company maintains cash and cash equivalents with various major financial institutions. Concentrations of credit risk with respect to receivables are generally limited due to the Company&#8217;s large number of customers and their dispersion across many countries and industries. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, the Company had <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant concentrations of credit risk.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Geographic Concentrations</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, a significant percentage of the Company&#8217;s cash and cash equivalents are held outside the United States. See the following table for the percentage of cash and cash equivalents by region of subsidiary, at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>:</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">13</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Segment and Geographic Data</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">VPG reports in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140654380">three</span> reportable segments: Sensors segment, Weighing Solutions segment, and Measurement Systems segment. The Sensors reporting segment is comprised of the foil resistor and strain gage operating segments. The Weighing Solutions segment is comprised of specialized modules and systems used to precisely measure weight, force torque, and pressure. The Measurement Systems reporting segment is comprised of highly specialized systems for steel production, materials development, and safety testing.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The chief operating decision maker ("CODM") is our chief executive officer. The evaluation of the segments performance is based on multiple performance measures including revenues and operating income, exclusive of certain items. Management believes that evaluating segment performance, excluding items such as restructuring severance, impairment of goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets and amortization of intangible assets, acquisition costs, and other items is meaningful because they relate to occurrences or events that are outside of our core operations, and management believes that the use of these measures provides a consistent basis to evaluate our operating profitability and performance trends across comparable periods.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The accounting policies of the segments are the same as those described in the summary of significant accounting policies (see Note <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>). Reporting segment assets are the owned or allocated assets used by each segment. Products are transferred between segments on a basis intended to reflect, as nearly as practicable, the market value of the products.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Israeli Severance Pay</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Israeli Severance Pay Law, <em style="font: inherit;">1963</em> ("Severance Pay Law"), specifies that employees of our Israeli subsidiary are entitled to severance payment, following the termination of their employment. Under the Severance Pay Law, the severance payment is calculated as <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-month salary for each year of employment, or a portion thereof.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Part of the subsidiary's liability for severance pay is covered by the provisions of Section <em style="font: inherit;">14</em> of the Severance Pay Law ("Section <em style="font: inherit;">14"</em>). Under Section <em style="font: inherit;">14,</em> employees are entitled to monthly deposits, at a rate of <em style="font: inherit;">8.33%</em> of their monthly salary, contributed on their behalf to their insurance funds. Payments in accordance with Section <em style="font: inherit;">14</em> release the subsidiary from any future severance payments in respect of those employees. As a result, the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognize any liability for severance pay due to these employees and the deposits under Section <em style="font: inherit;">14</em> are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recorded as an asset in the Company's balance sheet.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">For the subsidiary's employees in Israel who are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to Section <em style="font: inherit;">14,</em> the Company calculated the liability for severance pay pursuant to the Severance Pay Law based on the most recent salary of these employees multiplied by the number of years of employment as of the balance sheet date.&#160; The Company recorded as expenses the increase in the severance liability, net of earnings (losses) from the related investment fund.&#160; The subsidiary's liability was partially funded by monthly payments deposited with insurers and the value of these deposits is recorded as an asset on the Company's balance sheet.&#160;&#160; Any unfunded amounts would be paid from operating funds and are covered by a provision established by the subsidiary. The accompanying consolidated balance sheets at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em> include a $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654405" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherNoncurrentLiabilitiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccrualForTaxesOtherThanIncomeTaxesCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">6.2</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654406" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherNoncurrentLiabilitiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccrualForTaxesOtherThanIncomeTaxesCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">6.2</ix:nonFraction> million non-current liability, respectively, associated with Israeli severance requirements in other liabilities and a $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654407" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherNoncurrentAssetsMember" unitRef="USD" name="vpg:SeveranceTaxAsset" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140654408" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherNoncurrentAssetsMember" unitRef="USD" name="vpg:SeveranceTaxAsset" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">5.0</ix:nonFraction> million non-current asset, respectively, associated with Israeli severance requirements in other assets.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c3114180" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Note <em style="font: inherit;">16</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Fair Value Measurements</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820,</em> <i>Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures,</i> establishes a valuation hierarchy of the inputs used to measure fair value. This hierarchy prioritizes the inputs to valuation techniques used to measure fair value into <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> broad levels. The following is a brief description of those <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels:</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1:</em> Observable inputs such as quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em> Inputs other than quoted prices that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. These include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets and quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em> Unobservable inputs that reflect the Company&#8217;s own assumptions.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">An asset or liability&#8217;s classification within the hierarchy is determined based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   </ix:continuation>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company maintains nonqualified trusts, referred to as &#8220;rabbi&#8221; trusts, to fund payments under deferred compensation and nonqualified pension plans. Rabbi trust assets consist primarily of marketable securities, classified as available-for-sale money market funds at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, and company-owned life insurance assets. The marketable securities held in the rabbi trusts are valued using quoted market prices on the last business day of the year. The company-owned life insurance assets are valued in consultation with the Company&#8217;s insurance brokers using the value of underlying assets of the insurance contracts. The fair value measurement of cash and cash equivalents held in the rabbi trust is considered a Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> measurement and the measurement of the company-owned life insurance assets is considered a Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> measurement within the fair value hierarchy.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The fair value of the long-term debt, excluding capitalized deferred financing costs at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em> approximates its carrying value, as the revolving debt and term loans are reset monthly based on current market rates, plus a base rate as specified in the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> Credit Agreement. The fair value measurement of long-term debt is considered a Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> measurement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s financial instruments include cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable, short-term notes payable, and accounts payable. The carrying amounts for these financial instruments reported in the consolidated balance sheets approximate their fair values.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#160;Note <em style="font: inherit;">17</em> </span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8211;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "> Related Party Transactions</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Following the spin-off from Vishay Intertechnology, Inc. on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 6, 2010, </em>VPG is an independent, publicly-traded company, and Vishay Intertechnology does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> retain any ownership interest in VPG, although a common group of stockholders control a significant portion of the voting power of each company and the companies have <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> common board members.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Subsequent to the spin-off, VPG and Vishay Intertechnology continue to share certain manufacturing locations. VPG owns <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> location in Japan at which it leases space to Vishay Intertechnology. Lease receipts related to the shared facility are immaterial.</p>
